title: Setting Recently Deposited Money Against the Shortfall
content:
Money that has recently reached an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is set against the shortfall within a ceiling. The figure read is the total of deposits posted to the account in the one calendar month ending on the instruction date.

1. **At least 2000.00 USD of deposits posted in that window.** The shortfall is reduced by those deposits up to a ceiling of 400.00 USD, and never below zero.
2. **At least 750.00 USD but less than 2000.00 USD of deposits posted in that window.** The shortfall is reduced by those deposits up to a ceiling of 200.00 USD, and never below zero.
3. **Less than 750.00 USD of deposits posted in that window.** No deposit already posted is set against the shortfall.

The ceiling caps the reduction, not the deposits: where the deposits exceed the ceiling, the reduction is the ceiling figure, and where they fall below it, the reduction is the deposits themselves.

### Worked cases on a hypothetical shortfall

Take a shortfall of 900.00 USD.

| Deposits in the one calendar month ending on the instruction date | Reduction | Shortfall after the reduction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3000.00 USD | 400.00 USD, the ceiling of the first rule | 500.00 USD |
| 2000.00 USD | 400.00 USD, the ceiling of the first rule | 500.00 USD |
| 900.00 USD | 200.00 USD, the ceiling of the second rule | 700.00 USD |
| 750.00 USD | 200.00 USD, the ceiling of the second rule | 700.00 USD |
| 600.00 USD | none | 900.00 USD |

Where the shortfall is smaller than the reduction — say a shortfall of 150.00 USD against deposits of 3000.00 USD — the reduced figure is held at zero rather than going below it.

### Boundary of the figures

Deposits of exactly 2000.00 USD fall under the first rule, exactly 750.00 USD under the second, and 749.99 USD under the third.
